title: Skill Dashboard
summary: Creates, updates, checks and publishes a skill sheet: a vibe-dashboard page that explains one of Swami's own Claude skills, built from a skill card with a fingerprint that shows when the page is out of date.
what_it_is: Every one of Swami's own skills gets a **skill sheet**, a vibe-dashboard page in a fixed shape that explains what the skill is, how to use it on macOS and Windows, what it depends on, where it runs, and its gotchas. This skill makes those pages. Each one is rendered from a **skill card**, a JSON file holding the facts about the skill plus a **fingerprint** of its files.

The fingerprint is what keeps the pages honest: when any file in a skill changes, its fingerprint changes, so a later check (or the Skill Library's nightly refresh) can flag the page as out of date. Swami vets every page before it goes public. The skill only ever makes a private draft; nothing goes to GitHub until he says "publish" for that skill.
why: Swami shares his skills with other people, including Windows users. A skill sheet tells them what a skill does and what it needs before they install it, and the fingerprint means a stale page is caught instead of quietly drifting from the skill it describes.

what_it_does.text: Reads every file in the skill, fingerprints it, writes the card, builds the page, records the audio overview, checks it in a browser, and publishes a **private draft** artifact titled "<Title> skill".
Re-reads a skill that changed, updates only what the change affects (keeping Swami's edits and answers), and republishes the draft to the same link.
Compares every card's fingerprint with the skill as it is now and replies with a table: fresh, out of date, no dashboard yet, or skill missing.
After Swami's go, marks the card published and commits the page, card and narration to `dashboards/<skill>/` in the public `claude-skills` repo, where GitHub Pages serves it.
Every sheet has the same 16 sections in the same order, from Dashboard Summary and Search to Where It Runs, Gotchas, Card and Freshness, Mind Map, Glossary and the skill's own SKILL.md word for word.
Every card covers macOS and Windows: Windows install notes for each program, Windows steps, and Windows gotchas and requirements.
Anything it could not confirm from the skill's files goes in the card's `confirm` list and shows on the draft until Swami answers. A sheet can't be published while that list is open.
Keeps `dashboards/index.json`, the list of published sheets with their fingerprints, which the Skill Library reads every night to show each sheet's link and an out-of-date flag.
Runs vibe-dashboard's privacy scan on the page, card and narration before every publish and commit, so no one under NDA is ever named.

triggers: "Which skill dashboards are out of date?"

how_to_use.step: In a Claude chat on the Mac (desktop app or web), name the skill and the mode, for example "make a dashboard for youtube-comments".
Loads vibe-dashboard, reads every file in the skill, fingerprints it and writes the skill card, with open questions in `confirm`.
Runs `build_skill_sheet.py`: fills the template, applies the table-fit, Search and Mind Map patches, and writes a narration draft.
Audits the narration for noun and verb stress, fixes it in the card, and records the audio overview with the Kokoro voice.
Opens the page in a headless browser at 1000 and 1440 pixels wide: no console warnings, every summary row linked, no unused glossary term, tables fit. Runs the privacy scan.
Publishes the page as a private artifact with `card.txt` and `narration.txt` beside it, and lists the open questions in chat.
Opens the draft, answers the questions, and says "publish <skill>" when it's right.
Folds in the answers, rebuilds, commits to the `claude-skills` repo, and verifies the push. The Skill Library shows the link after its next nightly run.

how_to_use_windows.step: Same as on the Mac: in the Claude desktop app or claude.ai in Edge or Chrome, name the skill and the mode. Nothing runs on the PC itself.
Identical to macOS steps 2 to 6 and 8: everything runs in Claude's workspace, on claude.ai and on GitHub.
Open the draft in Edge or Chrome, answer the questions, and say "publish <skill>".

capabilities.text: The builder takes vibe-dashboard's patches from its current SKILL.md, so a rebuild picks up the latest Search, Mind Map and table-fit behavior.
Any change to any file in a skill changes its fingerprint, so check mode and the Skill Library's nightly refresh both catch an out-of-date sheet.
Each draft carries its card and narration as published files, so a later session can rebuild it without starting over.
The Skill Library's "How the Skills Connect" section reads each published card's skill dependencies, with the reason for each link.
Nothing goes public without Swami's "publish", and the privacy scan runs before every commit.

limitations.text: One skill per run unless Swami asks for more.
Made for Swami's own skills (Customize › Skills › Yours) and his repo; it does not document Anthropic's built-in skills.
Skill sheets have no owner-only audio refresh button, because the public copy lives on GitHub Pages, where it can't work. Update mode re-records the audio instead.
It never invents results: anything nobody has tried, such as a skill on Windows or in another AI, is marked Untested.
After Swami uploads a changed skill, Claude's synced copy can lag by up to about half an hour, so a fresh fingerprint may still show the old version.

scheduled_tasks.summary: None of its own. The Skill Library's nightly refresh reads this skill's registry to show each sheet's link and out-of-date flag.

tasks.name: Skills dashboard nightly refresh
tasks.what: Rebuilds the Skill Library. Its Dashboard column links each published sheet from `dashboards/index.json` and flags it out of date when the skill's fingerprint has changed.

other_ais.notes: Skills need a Business, Enterprise, Edu or Healthcare plan. With code execution and vibe-dashboard installed it could build the HTML page, but not claude.ai drafts or the GitHub publish.
Upload the unzipped folder plus vibe-dashboard. Same limits: a page file at best, no drafts or publishing.
Import the .zip, or the SKILL.md if refused; installing by chat drifts, and the scripts in its scripts folder are easy to lose.

gotchas.text: Before creating a draft, check `dashboards/index.json` and the artifact list for one that already exists; a second draft of the same skill causes confusion about which to publish.
Card text must not contain double curly braces: the builder treats them as unfilled template placeholders and stops.
Glossary `match` patterns must use non-capturing groups such as `(?:es)?`. A capturing group breaks the page's term matcher, so the build stops on one.
Files published beside a draft must come from the scratchpad or working directory, or the publish is refused.
github.io can be blocked from Claude's workspace, so check a published sheet through raw.githubusercontent.com instead.
Publishing a draft warns that the page uses `mcp` without declaring it. That's the audio player's unused refresh code; sheets declare no capabilities, so ignore it.
Fix wrong noun or verb stress in the card's `spoken` block, not just the narration file, or the next rebuild brings the mistake back.

requirements.text: Claude's GitHub access with push rights to `swami-claude-skills/claude-skills`, and GitHub Pages turned on for it.
Code execution with network access (GitHub, and the voice model the first time), and artifacts.
Swami's memory naming the people under NDA, for the privacy scan.
Any Mac (macOS) or Windows 10 or 11 PC with a browser, to vet drafts. Nothing is installed on it.

spoken._intro: This page is the skill sheet for the skill dashboard skill. It creates, [updates](/ʌpdˈeɪts/), checks and publishes a skill sheet: a vibe dashboard page explaining one of Swami's own skills, built from a skill card with a fingerprint that shows when the page is out of date
spoken.What It Is: Every one of Swami's skills gets a sheet in a fixed shape, rendered from a card. The card's fingerprint changes whenever the skill does, and nothing goes public until Swami says publish
spoken.What It Does: Nine jobs: create, [update](/ʌpdˈeɪt/), check and publish, the fixed sections, both Mac and Windows, open questions, the registry, and the privacy scan
spoken.How to Use It: Eight steps: ask, then Claude writes the card, builds, [records](/ɹᵻkˈɔːɹdz/), checks and publishes a private draft. Swami vets it and says publish. On Windows the steps are the same
spoken.Skills It Depends On: Vibe dashboard is required for the template, patches and audio. Artifact sharing audit is related, because it uses the same fingerprint
spoken.Programs It Depends On: Only a browser on your computer. Python, git, a headless browser and the [Kokoro](/kˈoʊkoʊɹoʊ/) voice run in Claude's workspace, and GitHub Pages serves the published sheets
spoken.Capabilities and Limitations: It stays current with vibe dashboard, flags stale pages, and keeps drafts rebuildable. But it works one skill at a time, only on Swami's skills, and never claims what nobody has tried
spoken.Scheduled Tasks: None of its own. The skill library's nightly refresh reads its registry to link each sheet and flag stale ones
spoken.Where It Runs: It runs in Claude's cloud sessions and in the desktop app on Swami's Mac, where every sheet so far was made. The other surfaces are untested
spoken.Gotchas: Seven traps, from duplicate drafts, curly braces and capturing groups in cards to file paths, checking published pages, the capability warning, and fixing stress in the card
spoken.Other Requirements: GitHub access to the claude skills repo, code execution with network access, Swami's memory of who is under NDA, and any Mac or Windows computer with a browser
spoken.Card and Freshness: Which version of the skill this page describes, and its fingerprint. There are no open questions
